concept.title: Metadata and social sharing
concept.shortdesc: Every page carries metadata in its head, read from the DITA: the tags that link previews, catalogues and search engines read. Nothing is invented; a value the DITA does not give is left out.

conbody.p: metadataOpen GraphDublin CoreWith the default govuk.metadata=basic, each page has Open Graph tags, which decide how a link to it looks when shared; Dublin Core tags, which government and library catalogues read; and links to its own address, its neighbours in reading order and its licence. govuk.metadata=no writes none of them. The print document never carries any.

section.title: What each page carries, and where it comes from

row.entry: Tags
Read from
og:title, DC.title
The topic's title. On the home page, the map's title (a bookmap's mainbooktitle).
og:description, DC.description
The topic's shortdesc, else the shortdesc in its topicref. On the home page, the map's shortdesc or the bookmap's booktitlealt.
og:locale, DC.language
The topic's xml:lang, else the map's.
website on the home page, article elsewhere.
govuk.service.name, else the map's title.
The title of the top-level entry of the navigation the page is under.
The topic's category and keyword elements. A keyword that only repeats a word of the page's title is not a tag, and each tag is written once.
article:published_time, article:modified_time
The topic's own critdates, only when govuk.dates shows dates. Dates in a bookmap's bookmeta date the book: the toolkit copies them to every topic, so they are not used for a page.
govuk.organisation, else the bookmap's publisherinformation organization, else the bookowner organization.
The publishing organisation. With govuk.metadata.persons=yes, the topic's (or the bookmap's) author elements instead.
What the footer says: Crown copyright for official branding, else govuk.footer.licence, else the bookmap's bookrights.
The Open Government Licence for official branding, else govuk.licence.url.
link rel="canonical", og:url, link rel="prev" and "next"
The page's address, and its neighbours' in reading order, under govuk.site.url. Without it they are left out, since the plugin has no other way to know the site's address.
govuk.og.image: an absolute URL, or a path under the site root, which needs govuk.site.url.
Always summary; the other values are read from the Open Graph tags.

section.title: Any other property: data elements
section.p: metadatadata elementA <data name="prefix:term" value="…"/> in a bookmap's bookmeta, the topicmeta of a map or an entry, or a topic's prolog states a property in a published vocabulary. The prefixes are dct (Dublin Core terms), dcat, adms, skos, rdf, foaf, org, vcard, schema and og.

ul.li: A property reaches every tag that is read from it. The example adds an article:tag.
A correct term that nothing at this level reads, such as dct:spatial, is kept for the catalogue outputs to come, and is not written.
A name that is not a term of those vocabularies, such as a misspelt dct:spacial, is reported once per build (GOVK011W) and left out.
A data element whose name has no prefix is the publisher's own, and is not metadata.

section.p: A page states its own properties first, from the entries above it in the map and then from its prolog. It takes the rest from the publication, except the properties that describe one thing only: its title, description, identifier, type, subjects and dates. A system that generates DITA should follow the guide for source systems.

section.title: Checking
section.p: A page the metadata tables require a value for, and that has none, is reported once per build for all such pages (GOVK012W). To look at a published page as a link preview will, use a social network's sharing debugger, or read the page's source. The repository's tools/check_metadata.py checks a built site against the same tables offline.
